name: CR-Diff-02-linearity-4.c
questiontext:
Expand the following expresion and differentiate it with respect to {{CT:0}}:\[ {{CT:1}}. \]

 [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
In order to solve this problem we will have to use the linearity rules for differentition. <hint>calc_diff_linearity_rule</hint>

 Since

 \[{{CT:1}}={{CT:2}},\]

 \[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
 \frac{d}{d{{CT:3}}}\left[ {{CT:1}}\right]  &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \frac{d}{d{{CT:3}}}\left( {{CT:2}}\right)  \\
    &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \frac{d}{d{{CT:3}}}\left( {{CT:4}}\right) + \frac{d}{d{{CT:3}}}\left( {{CT:5}}\right) + \frac{d}{d{{CT:3}}}\left( {{CT:6}}\right) + \frac{d}{d{{CT:3}}}\left( {{CT:7}}\right)  \\
    &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:8}}\frac{d}{d{{CT:3}}}\left( {{CT:9}}\right) + {{CT:10}}\frac{d}{d{{CT:3}}}\left( {{CT:11}}\right) + [{{CT:12}}]\frac{d}{d{{CT:3}}}\left( {{CT:13}}\right) + 0  \\
    &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:8}}\left[{{CT:14}}\right] + ({{CT:10}}){{CT:15}} + [{{CT:12}}]\left[{{CT:16}}\right] \\
    &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:17}} + {{CT:18}} + {{CT:19}}
  \end{array}\]

on_true.feedback: You seem to have used the sum rule to differentiate a product. Use to product rule instead <hint>calc_product_rule</hint>.

The derivative of a product is not the product of the derivative of each factor seperately.

 To differentiate a product you need to use the product rule <hint>calc_product_rule</hint>.
